title: The Beginner's Hands-On Guide to AI: 50 Hands-On Projects That Work With Any AI Tool -Taki
description: AI isn't just for tech people. It's for you. Maybe you've nodded along while friends raved about AI, quietly hoping nobody asks what you think. Or you opened a chatbot once, got a bland answer, and decided it wasn't for you. This book was written for you — and no, you're not too late. The Beginner's Hands-On Guide to AI is an AI for beginners book that skips the jargon, the math, and the code. Instead of reading about artificial intelligence, you learn AI by doing: 50 short, hands-on projects you complete with a real AI tool — each taking just minutes a day, on a free account, in whatever language you think in. You will learn to: Give clear instructions to any AI tool - ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot or whatever launches next year - in 60 seconds using the 5-Part Prompt Formula Spot made-up answers and fact-check anything in 60 seconds Use AI for everyday life, work, research, and creativity — including images, audio, and video Build your personal prompt library, then prove your progress with a 7-day final challenge This book is for you if you're a busy parent, a career changer, a curious retiree, or the professional who keeps meaning to "look into AI." You don't need to be good with technology — a phone or computer and a few minutes a day are enough. It's not for you if you want to code, study algorithms, or chase a technical certification. There are excellent books for that. This isn't one of them. Works with any AI tool — today and tomorrow. Every project runs on a free account: no paid plan, no workarounds, wherever you live. And when the tools change (they will), your skills won't expire — prompting, verifying, and iterating transfer to whatever comes next. title: Mechanical Cardboard Engineering for Beginners: 20 Hands-On Projects to Build Gears, Machi
description: Turn Ordinary Cardboard into Extraordinary Mechanical Creations! Have you ever wondered how gears turn, linkages move, or simple machines transform motion? With Mechanical Cardboard Engineering for Beginners, you can explore these fascinating principles through practical, hands-on projects using accessible materials. Whether you’re a curious beginner, a student, an educator, or a creative maker, this guide helps you turn everyday cardboard into working mechanical models while developing your understanding of motion, structure, and mechanical design. Inside, you’ll explore how to: Build cardboard gears, pulleys, and wheel-and-axle mechanisms. Create crank-and-slider machines, cams, and moving automata. Experiment with linkages, mechanical arms, and walking machines. Construct a miniature conveyor and combine multiple mechanisms. Improve stability, troubleshoot movement, and customize your own designs. With practical instructions, clear measurements, and engaging projects, you’ll learn by building, testing, and improving—not just by reading theory. Your next great engineering idea could begin with a simple piece of cardboard. Grab your materials, get creative, and start building! This book is intended for educational and informational purposes only. Projects are designed primarily for light-duty demonstration and experimentation.
